acme_customer: Hey team — since last night ~4% of our /v1/generate streaming calls end mid-json. No "finish_reason" and client parse fails. Happening across regions. Repro below.

mike_support: Sorry about that — can you paste the exact curl you used and the raw response (headers+body)? Also SDK/version?

acme_customer: curl --no-progress-meter -N -H "Authorization: Bearer xoxr-REDACTED" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
Response (truncated):
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
cache-control: no-cache
X-Request-ID: 01FZQ2XXXX

data: {"id":"resp_123","object":"stream","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"Hello"},"index":0}]}
data: {"id":"resp_123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":" world"}}]}
data: {"id":"resp_123","choices":[{"delta":{"content":"!"}}]}
data: {"id":"resp_123","choices":[{"delta":{}}, {"finish_reason":
<connection closed by server>

The payload ends mid-object, missing the trailing fields (finish_reason and closing braces).

mike_support: Thanks — can you confirm whether you are using token rotation mid-request (refreshing Authorization header while connection open)? Also do you pass through any CDN/proxy?

acme_customer: We rotate tokens periodically; the requests are routed through our Fastly edge and then to Redwood (we see X-Edge-Request-ID forwarded). Token rotation usually happens via short-lived creds.

mike_support: I'm escalating to engineering + SRE. Filing an internal trace now.

amanda_eng: Looking. Two quick asks to repro and collect extra info: 1) can you run the same curl but with --http1.1 to rule out HTTP/2 multiplexing behavior? 2) capture raw bytes with tcpdump or run: 
```
curl -v --http1.1 -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -H "Accept: text/event-stream" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate > resp.raw
```
then attach resp.raw. Also include the X-Request-ID.

acme_customer: OK attached resp.raw and X-Request-ID: 01FZQ2XXXX. Using --http1.1 reduces frequency but still reproduces once in a while.

edgebot: Fastly log for 01FZQ2XXXX: backend_response: 200, backend_status: 200, restart=1, bereq_body_bytes=0, beresp_body_bytes=1832, beresp_status=200, beresp_reason=OK, reason: backend fetch incomplete

raj_sre: From the logs the backend connection to the origin closed early with a truncated body for a subset of long-lived streams. Correlation with token refresh is plausible: if the client reuses a connection after rotating auth in front of Fastly or our ALB, middle proxy may try to re-open/hand off the stream causing the origin to terminate the TCP stream prematurely.

amanda_eng: Repro hypothesis: when a token rotation causes an intermediate client to initiate a new TLS session / connection reuse pattern while the origin is still streaming, the edge/proxy can issue a backend handoff and not wait for the final flush from the origin process. This results in the last SSE event (the closing JSON with finish_reason) never being relayed.

mike_support: Can you share the minimal mitigation we can advise the customer to test now?

amanda_eng: Quick workarounds to try: 1) avoid rotating tokens mid-stream (rotate only between requests) 2) set Connection: close on the request to force no reuse, e.g., 
```
curl -v -H "Connection: close" -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -N https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
3) set HTTP/1.1 (we observed slightly lower rate) 4) if behind Fastly/edge, add `streaming_keepalive` config or increase `send_timeout` on the CDN. We'll also try server side fixes.

acme_customer: Setting Connection: close eliminated the truncated responses in our quick test. Thank you.

amanda_eng: Engineering action items:
- Short-term: Document the SDK guidance to avoid in-flight token refresh and recommend `Connection: close` as a fallback.
- Mid-term: Update runtime to explicitly flush final SSE event and set TCP socket linger to ensure fin/psh until backend ack.
- Ops: Coordinate with CDN team to tune keepalive/send timeouts for streaming endpoints; ensure handoff won't drop tail bytes.

deploybot: Created ticket INF-2179 (internal) linking trace X-Request-ID 01FZQ2XXXX and Fastly log. Assigned to eng-runtime and eng-sre.

raj_sre: We'll also add an edge rule to avoid reusing backend connections for streaming routes for now. That should prevent the premature backend handoff while we implement the runtime flush.

mike_support: I'll reply to the customer with the `Connection: close` workaround and ETA for docs/patch. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

acme_customer: Appreciate the quick triage — happy to test any patch or canary.

amanda_eng: Thanks — we'll post updates in this thread when INF-2179 hits canary and once we've validated the fix.

mike_support: marking as escalated -> eng-runtime. Closing loop in support once patch verified.
